definitions.explanation: The empty space around text or images on a page; unused area left intentionally in documents, art, or design.
Space or capacity for something additional; breathing room in one's life or schedule.

notes:
{余白|よはく} means blank/white space, either literally or figuratively.

ETYMOLOGY:
{余|よ} (extra, surplus) + {白|はく} (white) - extra white space.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {余白|よはく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧ - to leave margins
- {余白|よはく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{設定|せってい}→設定：04767_settei⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ - to set margins
- {余白|よはく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧ - to write in the margin
- {余白|よはく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{活|い}かす→活かす：10422_ikasu⟧ - to make use of white space

CULTURAL NOTE:
Deliberate empty space is an important concept in Japanese aesthetics. In traditional arts like calligraphy, ⟦{日本画|にほんが}→日本画：18225_nihonga⟧, and garden design, the space left unfilled is valued as much as the filled areas. {余白|よはく} is the concrete term for that space on a page or canvas; the broader aesthetic principle of meaningful emptiness — in space, in time, in conversation — is called {間|ま} (a separate word from ⟦{間|あいだ}→間：00914_aida⟧ 'interval', though written with the same kanji).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {余白|よはく} vs. マージン: much the same meaning; マージン is the loanword, used mainly in page-layout software and printing
- {余白|よはく} vs. ⟦{空白|くうはく}→空白：15426_kuuhaku⟧: {余白|よはく} is the intentional margin around content; ⟦{空白|くうはく}→空白：15426_kuuhaku⟧ emphasizes emptiness itself and can be an unintended gap (a blank in a form, a gap in a career)
